claims.says: Given codecs obeying their round-trip laws, decoding the single-key RDB payload of a well-formed graph gives exactly its restore arguments under any key name, and any truncation asks for more.
A well-formed graph saved across two or more keys and loaded in any key order reads back every key and ends with no pending graph, finalized to its single-key restore.
Every scalar property value encoded in the v19 RDB format decodes back to itself, leaving whatever follows it in the stream untouched.
In a multi-key save, the entity slices of all keys in key order list each kind's ids from 0 up exactly once, kinds in encoding order, when the entity total fits u64.
Two uuid_v4 results, used to name virtual keys, whose counters differ modulo 2^48 are always different, whatever the clock readings.
